notes.title: Free Major Update coming June 7th!
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

It’s been 4 months since our last update but we’ve been cooking because Pyrene is about to extend its territory… 

Ever heard of French Brittany? Bretons? You’ll find out about its myths and legends through the new major update on June 7th!

[previewyoutube=5rMymjyCKX0;full][/previewyoutube]

And, we’ll have a 24hr-Daily Deal on June 7th, the discount will last 7 days so hopefully more players can pick up Pyrene and try it out. Tell your friends about the upcoming discount!

Without further ado, here is what you can expect from the update:

Note: the update picks up after the base game story!

Update Content

4 New biomes

 Whispering Woods - So eerie, it might even bring monsters back to life.
 Wild Moor - A place that will keep you stuck in its pouring rain.
 Granite Shore - Wade across the tide, but beware of the electric eels.
 Twilight Field - Only the bold and the well-prepared will survive this endless night. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44387931/ec99c03a1db1274b5c3ecb1c6e936687c98e5d47.png

5 New Playable Characters

 Malo the Mana User - A young sorcerer wielding a mana-powered hand of cards.

… and 2 other secret ones!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44387931/d4388e54ed754ffcdd913d4857067a51634b8c89.png

 Yuna
 Keridwen

… and a last one, that you’ll unlock under certain conditions!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44387931/ae22aef9e94610849e26116af1783e0d1a654052.png

And 2 new Herensuge challenges for each playable character!

Chinese localization

notes.content:
Hello everyone,

We're back with a little patch that addresses the following:


Bug fixes

 Fixed a bug preventing you from leaving an expedition under certain conditions (which caused the game to softlock).
 Fixed a bug with Torque and Divine Fruit cards that generated an infinite Echo loop.
 Cards no longer overlap when generating cards in the biome first zone.
 The 5th biome selected in level 3 of the workshop is no longer ignored.
 Isop no longer appears in the steles zone when no longer required.

Features

 Powers that open an interface now interact with “Sigil” relics.
 Increased health for the last boss in the game's story.
 Some watchtower relics only appear once the associated feature (such as luck) has been unlocked.
 A new relic has been added to the watchtower, in late game, allowing you to reroll with gold instead of wood.

notes.title: 1.02 Update | Small fixes & Balancing
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

We're back with a little patch that addresses the following:

BUG FIXES AND BALANCING

Miscellaneous

 It is no longer mandatory to collect all the cards in the zone to change biome when the main story is over.
 Chest opening animation has been greatly optimized.
 More Steam achievements are checked when loading the save game.
 Cards given by Andos now display a description with the correct value.
 The “Corrupted Wood” card has been removed from the list of cards in the warehouse collection.
 Free mode allows you to launch an expedition with the selected character.
 Gashia's bear form can no longer increase the rage bar.
 Millaris no longer increases Gashia's HP.
 Text corrections


Cards

 The “Pure Water Potion” card no longer triggers powers that open an interface.
 The “Blue Crystal” card can now receive echo.
 The “Divine Fruit” card can now receive echo.
 The “Cervoise” card no longer crashes when there are no cards to duplicate.


Relics

 The “Golden Chalice” relic now gives +2 to loot cards rather than +3.
 The “Red Helmet” relic now gives shield when the enemy takes bleeding damage rather than when it receives the status.
 The “Silver Chalice” relic no longer gives shield with the “Iron Bracelet” relic.
 The “Broken Chalice” relic no longer prevents you from obtaining a “Votive Altar” card in the Mairu Totem zone.
 The “Ethereal Feather” relic no longer reduces the dodge value of the “Ethereal Knife” card by -2.
 The “Burning Tooth” relic can no longer be duplicated.


Powers

 The “Perfect Copy” power increases its cost by +1 spirit after each use.
 The “Telekinesis” power increases its cost by +1 spirit after each use.
 The “Illumination” power increases its cost by +1 spirit after each use (instead of +2 previously).
 The “Lyre” power cost increased from 8 to 12 spirits.
 The “Shield Conversion” power generates cards on which you can move.
 The “Spark” power generates cards on which you can move.

notes.title: 1.01 is LIVE NOW!
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

Thank you very much for the feedback provided on the testing branch!

Here's a list of all the changes made so far:

=============================

Characters

Mathilda:

 Mathilda now has a “Basic Shield" stat that can be increased thanks to Holy Plant cards.
 Her HP increase from 4 to 5.
 Her deck starts with a “Golden Apple” card.
 Her default power is now “Sliding”.


Gashia:

 Gashia has a new “Spiritual Plant” relic that reduces the cost of her powers by -1 spirit per Holy Plant collected.
 Her HP increases from 10 to 12.
 Her “Bear Statuette” card now triggers the burn status of enemies in play. Its value drops from 5 to 3.
 The default spirit cost of her powers is higher.
 The “Simple Ring” card in her deck has been replaced by a “Fire Staff” card.


Tanegui:

 Tanegui has a new “Sparkling Stones” power that generates gold coin cards.


Balancing
Global:

 Chests require higher values for epic and legendary items (the best possible chest remains at 18).
 Bosses have more HP.
 Addition of a “Dead Luck” relic in the watchtower, which disables the chance stat.
 The gold price of anvils has been slightly increased.
 Relics sold by Hadetta (“Sigil” relics) are more expensive.
 Tantugou now sells unique and high-powered relics.


Cards:

 The “Whetstone” card now gives +1 to N cards in play permanently (rather than +N to 1 card). It has been upgraded from rare to epic.
 The “Ring of Ekhi” card conditions the generation of a Holy card to a number of HP.
 The “Invisibility Potion” card still gives the same amount of dodge, but then reduces HP to 1.
 The “Blue Crystal” card now deals 1 damage without the possibility of being upgraded.
 The “Ethereal Shield” card has been upgraded from legendary to epic.
 The “Thorny Plant” card has been upgraded from common to rare.
 The "Scales” card upgraded from common to rare.
 The "Invisibility Cloak” card value was reduced from 3 to 2.
 The “Red Cloak” card changes from a value of 2 to 1.


Relics:

 The 4 “Sigil” relics that inflict status when using a power now target a single enemy rather than all of them.
 The “Sigil of Protection” relic only triggers with powers costing 3 spirits or more.
 The “Sigil of Agility” relic now gives 2 dodges instead of 3.
 The “Enhancement Ring” relic is now unlocked by visiting 11 biomes (rather than by obtaining 6 steles).
 The “Precious Skull” relic no longer causes enemies to attack if they have died in the meantime.
 The “Sigil of Improvement” relic now confers a +1 rather than a +3 bonus.
 The “Ether Sigil” relic no longer triggers powers that open an interface. It has been upgraded from rare to legendary.
 The “Monster Meat”, “Monster Eyes” and “Red Helmet” relics now give 1 resource.
 The “Fire Stone” relic now deals 4 damage instead of 8.
 The “Scale Belt” relic upgraded from rare to epic.
 The “Feather” relic upgraded from common to rare.
 The “Iron Belt” relic upgraded from epic to legendary.
 The “Gold Belt” relic upgraded from common to rare.
 The “Elixir of Dodge” relic upgraded from epic to legendary.
 The “Garnet” relic upgraded from common to rare.
 The “Amethyst Belt” relic was downgraded from legendary to epic.
 The “Belt of Strength” relic was downgraded from legendary to epic.
 The “Invisibility Hood” relic was downgraded from epic to rare.
 The “Book of Demons” relic was downgraded from rare to common.
 The “Pine cone” relic was downgraded from legendary to rare.


Special powers:

 The dark forest power “Follow the Light” no longer triggers relic effects.
 The “Telekinesis” power can no longer target spirit cards.
 The “Rapid Attack” power can no longer be triggered automatically when dodging (this could generate an infinite loop).
 The “Stealth” power is now free, even under the “Curse” weather effect.
 The “Lenient Winds” power cost increased from 1 to 3 spirits.
 The “Lyre” power cost increased from 5 to 8 spirits.


Talismans:

 The “Talisman of Potion” no longer targets Zoè.
 The “Talisman of Metamorphosis” no longer invokes Zoè.
 The “Talisman of Wealth” now works as it should.


Interface

 The board reroll button is now positioned on the right of the screen.
 The 5th power is now correctly positioned after the others.
 It is now possible to leave an expedition from a chest.
 Unlocking the sanctuary now selects the correct number of powers.
 The Anvil can no longer be closed by mistake during hammer animation.
 Power costs are now correctly displayed on the character screen.
 It is no longer possible to submit the Pagomari screen several times.
 A text appears on the main screen indicating to click to continue.
 Various spelling and localization corrections.


Bug fixes

 The Steam achievement “All for One” can now be completed.
 The Steam achievement “Herensuge Challenges” can now be completed.
 The Steam achievement “Andos Legacy” now requires 5 items instead of 9.
 Dodge is correctly consumed with every attack.
 Holy cards are now generated correctly with Mathilda and Gashia.
 Akohan and Tanegui can select an additional power in the sanctuary.
 The “Windy Meadow” biome no longer triggers its wind effect when its weather effect has been removed with a card.


We hope you enjoy these new adjustments! Feel free to join our Discord and say what you think about the game by leaving a review!

The Two Tiny Dice team

Hello everyone,

First off: We cannot stress how happy we are with the launch of Pyrene! Thank you for welcoming the game with such enthusiasm and leaving your reviews!

We've tweaked and fixed some bugs you pointed out in the bug report forum on Discord, social media and reviews. Thank you for that.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44387931/63eec36ed99d918ec2e58bbd191429577554ab48.png

The testing branch is kind of like a test server where you can play a version of the game that includes fixes and tweaks before being officially patched and sent out to everyone. The preliminary changelog is in Discord but we'll post an official Steam news update to annonce the patch + post the entire changelog tomorrow or Wednesday.

If you want to see the changelog ahead of time. please feel free to join our Discord and share your thoughts so we're sure everything works fine and we can make it go live asap!

 Go to your library
 Right-click on the Pyrene app
 Select "Properties"

 Select "testing - Branch made for testing new changes" and close the window to launch the update.

notes.title: Dev Team Interviews - Game Design & Dev with Christophe!
notes.content:
Meet the people who have brought Pyrene to life in these short interviews!

Finally, let’s meet Christophe, head of Two Tiny Dice, who has operated Pyrene’s development. 

Are you satisfied with the balance between all the game's mechanics?

Yes!

I'm happy about the deckbuilding mechanics that create a path through the zones. This is a refreshing feature that works very well in my opinion. Combined with the greedy aspect of the Votive Altars that increase in value, it creates a good balance between risk and reward.

I like easy-access games, with few actions possible at the same time. For a while, I was scared that deck management, relics, powers and talismans would be too difficult to handle and make the game stodgy.

I've worked hard to ensure that these systems are easy to learn and non-invasive to the game's basic gameplay. You only have to deal with one thing at a time. For example, talismans are only managed when facing an Erge Altar. So, it's a game mechanic you don't need to think about the rest of the time. The same goes for relics in chests.

The number of choices at any given moment is always limited. But the total number of choices throughout a whole game is considerable. That's what makes the game so interesting and replayable, in my opinion.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44387931/a68efa3adb3f52f78e852827559dbb545e9b0020.gif

Pyrene is similar to your previous game Forward: Escape the Fold, yet so different. Which elements make them stand out from each other?

I'd say that Pyrene takes Forward's basic features but pushes them further while adding new ones, such as:

 A deck of cards to manage and improve
 More possibilities for movement and cards on the board
 Varied situations thanks to different biomes, weather effects, boss mechanics, etc.
 Meta-progression with a village to rebuild and upgrade to unlock content
 A "Luck" and "Affinities" system to guide the building of your deck
 Wider range of status effects with greater synergies
 Narration and the NPCs you meet
 Other secrets to discover 👀


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44387931/c967d9f8c0a836f84b9230dea5a0d82610128175.gif

How convenient is working with your own game engine? Did you find it smoother to work with the rest of the team?

It's very convenient to work with my own engine. What I particularly appreciate is working on interfaces, and traditional engines make this part very unsatisfactory in my opinion. With my own engine, I'm not afraid to add tooltips, tutorials, UI opening/closing animations, etc.

This has also allowed us to be quite free in combining tools used outside the engine. For the narration, for example, Marion could use the writing tool that suited her best, and I developed a system to import that into the game automatically. 

I think our work process is reliable from that point of view.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44387931/139b89174dedc3bde6ea0ad50bac18b59514d279.png

What makes you proud about Pyrene? What is the most important thing you've learned from the development?

What makes me proud? The innovative side of the game.

When we think of a roguelike deckbuilding game, we immediately think of Slay the Spire or any other game with a side view and a hand of cards at the bottom of the screen. Pyrene is a far cry from that, which was our intention from the start. I'm happy to have succeeded in keeping to this line throughout development. As for the gameplay, the concept I created 2 years ago is actually pretty close to the final game.

The most important thing I've learned? To work in a team—and ours worked out pretty well, which is amazing—and not to go into the red by working too much—that's the deal with this kind of job. That's two things, oops.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44387931/86214ee906f4002a6e8d1887c571e59a0acc24ae.gif

Pyrene will launch on September 13th, be ready to spread the word on our socials! Feel free to wishlist the game and join our Discord to share your excitement with us!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2468100/Pyrene/

notes.title: Dev Team Interviews - Narration with Marion!
notes.content:
Meet the people who have brought Pyrene to life in these short interviews!

Next up is Marion, who handled all the narration and settled the lore.

How much did you know about the Basque and Pyrenean mythology before diving into Pyrene?

In the Pyrenees, legends are everywhere, even if we don’t always pay attention to them. When I lived there for a few years, I noticed the mountain trails, street names and restaurants were often connected to local legends. But people get used to them, and the knowledge slowly fades away. Years later, as I was thinking about the world that would become Pyrene’s, I remembered these legends that had once piqued my curiosity. I started looking into them… and I realized there was so much more to them.

There’s such diversity and depth in these cultures — cultures so different from what we’re used to in video games, like the Greek, Nordic, or even Gallic and Celtic ones when we think of France. With Pyrene, we hope to introduce our players to the richness of Pyrenean and Basque mythologies, with their pantheons of gods, powerful imagery, and incredibly unique creatures. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44387931/b38618cd9543dd610dfc11cc57e75e498d2ff93b.png

The myths Pyrene is based on left few traces. How challenging was it to build up a solid narrative?

Quite challenging indeed! Like with most mythologies, even the well-documented ones, there are often many versions of the same event. We decided to do our own take on the myth of Pyrene and the creation of the Pyrenees, drawing from different sources and giving it a meaning that felt right to us. We also took some liberties, like combining creatures from different mythologies (Basque and Pyrenean cultures have some similarities but are based on different people and languages) or reimagining those with little to no historical information. What was really important to us was to represent and honor as many stories, legends, and creatures as we could. In a game that isn’t heavily focused on narration, our main goal was to create a consistent universe for players to explore, and maybe even inspire them to learn more about these cultures.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44387931/087a8236daab507a83df7b913d3992ed4b6428a3.png

How challenging was it to make the narration and the gameplay mechanics coexist?

It was tough but very rewarding! In a small team like ours, creation is a collaborative process. We talk a lot with Christophe to make sure the game design and narrative design are consistent and complement each other. We talk about a character's personality and background, like Mathilda, and then found a mechanic that fit her strength (and stubbornness). Other times, it was the opposite: we had an idea for a character mechanic inspired by a werewolf (I won’t say more to keep some element of surprise and make you want to play the game, hehe), and we thought about which character would “wear” it best, building the coherence and substance of that character around it. Being able to work on all of this as a team (and I love how our team works together) lets us bounce around ideas, making the work richer and definitely more fun!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44387931/a845da14ad961770fccfe576d1f3ea59e6996ce4.png

Which character or creature do you find the coolest and why?

Oh boy... All of them! I have to admit, I have a soft spot for the really unique creatures from Basque legends, like the Came-cruse or Idittu — two of Pyrene’s creatures that I’d love to have as plushies, even if they would clearly keep me up at night.

As for the characters, I remember the first time Jeanne sent us her sketches: after spending hours imagining their relationships, their mechanics, how they’d talk, seeing them come to life, each with their own expressions, poses, colors… it was pretty incredible. So I’m going to cheat and not choose just one because what I really love is how they all come together. The first idea of the game was to show a small group of regular people, not warriors, who go through extraordinary events and have to support each other to get through it. I really love the little community we’ve created, with characters that are so different, both visually and in their personalities and relationships. It makes the village feel more real and authentic, and I hope players will feel that too.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44387931/a63fb9c0dd0785ac1b66f77cd03272e6c6024721.png

Pyrene will launch on September 13th, be ready to spread the word on our socials! Feel free to wishlist the game and join our Discord to share your excitement with us!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2468100/Pyrene/

notes.title: Dev Team Interviews - Art & animation with Jeanne!
notes.content:
Meet the people who brought Pyrene to life in these short interviews!

We’re starting with Jeanne, who handled most of the art and animation in Pyrene.

What references from the myths have you based your designs on?

Basque myths were mostly passed on through word of mouth, so I had few visual references to help me. I had to find textual descriptions and use my own imagination to give life to most of Pyrene’s characters and creatures!

Basajaun and Basandere are wild, big and furry, Mamarroak are small, insect-like, with red pants.

For Babau, I was inspired by its representation on the Babau Festival’s floats!

It wasn’t an easy challenge but I had a lot of fun, as I always love creating creatures and discovering new ones!

According to you, what makes Pyrene unique, from an artistic point of view?

We made a strong choice for Pyrene’s artistic direction: roguelikes with fights against dangerous monsters are often set in a dark fantasy atmosphere. We chose to go in the opposite direction, with soft character designs, pastel and colorful palettes and natural environments. We wanted to give the feeling that these places aren’t scary to Pyrene’s villagers because it’s the land they’ve always known. We emphasized character’s expressions and animations, as their emotional journey is important to the game’s story.

Also, we acknowledged that Pyrene’s public won’t necessarily be hardcore roguelike players only but also people who care about narration and a diverse cast!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44387931/44e2e6d0cab14fa1c22b790f3ec06bcb49d9e2de.gif

Were there specific tasks that took you out of your comfort zone? Or on the contrary,  did you feel like your work fitted in with the game’s atmosphere?

I genuinely felt like my work fit in the project! My team was always very supportive of my choices and designs, I was and still am so thankful for that! I could really have fun with the visuals and make them match with both our project's gameplay and narration.

One of my initiatives was to animate each character and add their different expressions to their idles. I really felt it would make our game more lively and make the players feel what the villagers are going through. Plus, it was super fun to do!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44387931/f12bcc887a58f6d73755071956da41e8a0d7fa9a.gif

Is there a character you are obsessed with?

That’s a difficult question because I enjoy them so much! I can’t help myself but to speak about multiple ones:

 Atanaia, because she’s the first character we play and I love to play her. I drew her in many different other game artstyles and we even did a "Draw this in your style" with her, it was incredible!
 Mathilda is my favorite tall, strong and buff woman who knows how to handle a hammer.
 Hadetta because she probably has the design I love the most!
 Idittu because she is the quirkiest of all, and I do love the quirkiness
 …And of course Zoè, who is both a cute pet to have around and a fearless companion. She is adorable!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44387931/d5b5f9f73785d0059257d907a17dca4cd76c61e0.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44387931/fe05d6cbe9b62256a5ba3a5f22f2e5e7fc37444a.jpg
Atanaia as a character in Don't Starve, Cuphead and Darkest Dungeon!
Atanaia's design by Jeanne Prigent, Games by Klei Entertainment, Studio MDHR Entertainment Inc. and Red Hook Studios, Art direction by Jeff Agala, Andrea Fernandez and Chris Bourassa.

Which creature did you enjoy designing the most?

Now that you know me a little bit better, you know I won’t stick to one answer :

 The Drac, a reference to Berserk, is a disgusting one that I loved designing. it can have different forms depending on the region, but in the Pyrenees, it looks like a red demon donkey and I find it very original!
 The Creepy Unicorn, I always wanted to see an evil unicorn in a game and as I watch a lot of streams since Pyrene’s demo is out, I feel like players noticed how nasty it is.
 Iratxo, the evil little elf. I didn’t have a lot of description to work with, so I took liberties with its design! I included ferns as antennas, as its name refers to this plant! I think I’m really pleased with how it turned out!


{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44387931/33b0997360c5abfe0c56771d8ca58cbd1af274f1.png

Pyrene will launch on September 13th, be ready to spread the word on our socials! Feel free to join our Discord to share your excitement with us!

notes.title: August Devlog #3 | Put your cards on the table in Pyrene!
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

Along with our first devlog that shortly explains Pyrene’s gameplay, we wanted to share with you why, according to us, Pyrene bring something new to card-based games, through innovative and varied mechanics!

What genre is Pyrene exactly?

It’s always been challenging for us to describe what Pyrene is about. Over the months and years, we have concluded that the core of the gameplay is:

 Its fast pace as you crawl through various zones and biomes
 Solving the zones like a puzzle
 Replayability, through a permadeath system in which you keep your progression partly

And secondly comes:

 Extending, improving and rearranging your deck of cards!


Don’t get us wrong: cards remain essential in Pyrene! But, by putting the spotlight on the cards only, we miss out on many fundamental aspects.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44387931/9bba19204d7cbe929f65f5936ad46bff106af951.gif

What are the cards for then?

First off, most of the elements in the game are in the shape of cards. Characters, NPCs, enemies & bosses, buildings… Everything that appears on the tiles is card-shaped.

But we want to rather talk about the equipment cards! They play an essential role, since they’ll help you to define a strategy to defeat challenging creatures and bosses. Among the hundred of equipment cards, you’ll find:

 cards that cause damage or apply effects on enemies.
 cards that heal you and add resources (gold, spirit, supplies and so on).
 cards that shake up other cards – for example swapping position, pushing or mixing up other cards...
 corrupted cards that give you things but against a slight drawback.


Depending on the biome, you might need different cards with specific effects, while always trying to keep the balance of your health and supplies.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44387931/a4024d72215cced27da82de82809fe918a2c06b7.png

Managing your deck is key

As you’ll open chests and build a nice deck of cards, rearranging and improving them will be crucial! 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44387931/5af0add1a4bde0a5ecdac0bc3f030caf2e04ef38.gif

You’ll meet various NPCs and elements that allow you to do so: Jentil applies an effect on one card, Truffandec duplicates a card, the anvil will buff them against gold, the Erge Altar applies the effects of talismans on your deck.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44387931/83f2f8111f7e9585923d3cd19d143224768ddff3.gif

Don’t miss out on the release date announcement by joining our Discord and following our socials!

notes.title: July Devlog #2 | 3 mythical figures you’ll meet in Pyrene
notes.content:
As you know, Pyrene is deeply inspired by the myths from the Basque Country and the Pyrenees.

We thought you might be interested in a little spotlight on some of them and tell you about their background!

1. Jentil/Jentilak

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44387931/15d5093fce21f233c005d0404f312474fef133cb.png

Living in the mountains, these furry giants lived before the Christian era. The legends say they represented the Basque people. They were known to throw rocks at their enemies, but they’re above all protectors of the mountains!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44387931/9cedc9c6ee64f0468953026733f1a883dc2be86c.gif

Also… They have a sort of alter ego: the Basandere/Basajaun!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44387931/133e7c83ca06141b856b2984b1ea72e31dd8d0ac.png

Basandere is feminine, Basajaun, masculine.

They protect their forest, are more isolated. They are basically humans who were living a primitive lifestyle. They didn’t live in the same era as the Jentilak but are similar physically and in their role in the legends.

In Pyrene, we have decided to represent them more creature-ish, like corrupted Jentilak. You’ll fight these pitiless creatures in the danger zones!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44387931/628a20719bbb8cd780fdddee75222967dc91ed16.gif

2. Millaris

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44387931/216f386b11b81d248a194086d144e7abde5e412b.png

You can’t miss him out with his adorable boy, a Great Pyrenees!

Millaris is an old shepherd known to have provided the snow all across the Pyrenees! As it snowed for the first time, he knew he had the duty to spread it across the mountains. A duty he passed on to his sons, and it has snowed every year in this mountain range ever since.

You’ll meet Millaris as a merchant in Pyrene!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44387931/f12bcc887a58f6d73755071956da41e8a0d7fa9a.gif

3. Mamarro

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44387931/ff5ba494a0fafebb96d03fa8166e29aac3a2f4ca.png

Unlike the giant beings mentioned previously, Mamarroak are small protectors from the Basque land! It was said that you could summon these winged insects with a needle box, and they’d do anything to lighten your daily life.

Thanks to Mamarro, you can duplicate your relics in Pyrene!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44387931/4a250d3e3c20ac91b833aeb9fc7be39cd628a4fd.gif

What else would you like to know about Pyrene? Feel free to tell us in the comments!

Our Discord server also has a smoother setup to collect feedback and bugs, feel free to join it!

notes.title: July Devlog 🐍 Dive into Pyrene’s gameplay
notes.content:
For a while now, the main feedback we’ve been receiving from players is that they didn’t expect Pyrene to be *this* much fun. It is time for us to explain why Pyrene stands out and is in a league of its own!

The variety of objectives

Pyrene doesn't just rely on you surviving the furthest you can in a run - you also have to get your village back on its feet, unlocking new features in different biomes, characters, powers…

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44387931/d6938fe2dc83da82afe84062374954fdb87a1d71.gif

Increasing difficulty

When you launch a roguelike for the first time, you might feel frustrated about the immediate high-level difficulty at the start. What makes roguelikes fun is figuring out how to outsmart the game and finding your preferred playstyle and strategies to make it easier. In Pyrene, you’ll start with a "lower" difficulty, and you can even make the game easier if you feel overwhelmed. The more you progress into the zones and biomes and defeat bosses, the more difficult the game becomes.

Environmental effects will add up, creatures will become stronger with trickier passive effects, organizing your deck will become crucial…

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44387931/cc41b69be45eb140383cff321fd2bec6043d2d2c.gif

A puzzle-like fighting style

When you enter a danger zone, it's like a puzzle you have to solve. You’ll need to plan your moves - as you cannot go backward - continuously check your HP, use your special powers carefully, paying attention to the environmental conditions… And the “Spending the Night” mechanic also has pros and cons, so it’s more complex than slaying the monsters and moving on!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44387931/44e2e6d0cab14fa1c22b790f3ec06bcb49d9e2de.gif

We’d be happy to tell you more about the lore of the game, since Pyrene is also deeply narrative-oriented! Want to know more about something in particular? Leave a comment below! Feel free also to join our Discord server to ask us and stay informed about the latest news!

Join the Discord server here!

notes.title: Pyrene will be out in September!
notes.content:
Upgrade your deck, slay mythical creatures and find that Votive Altar - Pyrene will release in September 2024!

As we share this exciting news with you, we also wanted to let you know that we updated the demo ahead of Steam Next Fest. Here's what's changed:


 New weather effects
 New exploration points to unlock more zones
 New bosses with unique mechanics
 Simplified the watchtower. It's now an easy/accessible mode.
 Merchants are much cheaper
 Chests provide rarer content than before
 Rebalanced all the enemies in all the biomes (quantity, HP and passive effects).
 Added the possibility of seeing the details of the dungeon deck.
 Added the anvil to improve your cards
 Erge Altar (talismans) now uses gold instead of spirits (to not be "afraid" to use your powers).
 Added Pagomari to improve one affinity
 Added Andos, which gives us special (and very powerful) cards.
 Added a bunch of new relics, cards and talismans
 The village buildings are functional
 Added new comeback mechanics


Don't forget to wishlist the game to not miss out on its release and join the community on Discord and let us know your favorite part of the game!

notes.title: First Update - Demo changelog, Feedback and Upcoming events!
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

Just wanted to provide a first update with Pyrene.

Firstly, we're super excited to see the positive reception to the demo! It's a good validation that we're on the right track so thank you for that. Before we get into the feedback, here is a list of changes to the demo that we pushed on Monday:

CHANGELOG

Features

Enemies now drop a votive shard when the votive altar is in play. This is the new way to increase the altar.
10+ new layouts for danger zones.
After the first victory, you can now start a run by choosing the starting biome.
A relic now indicates the number of cards left to draw to find the votive altar. It will be available at the start of the game, in the watchtower.
You can now switch between Zoè and Akohan simply by clicking on the card.


Balancing

Frost, bleed and dodge statuses now decrease by 1 after each move.
Some cards had their effects changed because they were either too powerful or useless (including honey, divine fruit, iron ingot, fire flower, ethereal shield, healing herb...)
Fixed many bugs and balancing issues that made the game too easy to "break".


UI / UX

For greater clarity, in danger zones, empty spaces are marked as inaccessible.
The "spend the night" button is displayed in red when you take damage. And a skull when it's lethal.
To better identify them, cards from our deck are now marked with a small flag below their value.
It's now possible to hold down the click to add wood to a building.
Managing save slots is easier.



FEEDBACK

As mentioned before, we're incredibly happy with the inital reception and overall positive reviews that came from the demo. Although it's a good first validation, we know there's room to improve.

In order for us to build a better game, It's important to better understand why you liked it or didn't like it. That being said, we made an anonymous feedback form with some questions to know more about your experience. No question is mandatory but the more information you can give us, the more we can improve!

Here is the link to the feedback form


UPCOMING EVENTS

We can finally announce that we'll be in the #TurnBasedThursday fest next week!

https://i.imgur.com/7EozKii.png

We're hoping this can generate more eyes on our project and we're actively looking at other showcases to participate in to branch out.

We've applied to a bunch but this is the only one that is confirmed as of right now. We'll keep you all up to date whenever we are chosen for other showcases.

THANKS!

That's all for now! We're still hard at work on the game but we're keeping in touch with our community on social media, Steam and Discord. If you haven't done it yet, Join our Discord! We share announcements first on Discord and we love talking to you all whether it's to talk about the Pyrene/Forward, game development or games in general so if you have any questions, you know where to find us!

Thanks for your time and have a great day,
Two Tiny Dice
